consistency: CedarDB snapshot isolation and PostgreSQL REPEATABLE READ for mutation/read transactions. Analytical SELECTs are individually snapshot-consistent. No serializable, multi-writer conflict or general linearizability claim.
atomicity: Each two-row change and its receipt are one synchronous database transaction. Group count, amount sum and payload length stay fixed, while stored bodies and revisions genuinely change.
durability: Every connection sets/checks CedarDB async_commit=off or PostgreSQL synchronous_commit=on, fsync=on, full_page_writes=on. Retained-volume process/container crash is distinct from device/power loss.
retries: No mutation replay. All submitted errors remain ambiguous until native receipts and complete bodies are reconciled with fsynced external intents. Later requests use new sequence IDs.
deletes: Two rows are deleted and reinserted inside one transaction; readers must never see the transient missing pair. Permanent delete/TTL/reclamation workloads remain separate.

client.arrival: ticker-paced closed loop; missed ticks under backpressure are not queued
client.tls: disabled on the isolated lab network

data.types: BIGINT PK id; INTEGER customer/amount; TEXT payload; BIGINT revision
data.pattern: Each selected pair receives UPDATE then DELETE/reinsert; cycle through the configured pair window. Same analytical bucket, balanced signed amount adjustment, same payload length. One final pair remains historical and immutable.
data.payload: 192 bytes of repeated customer prefix plus 64 ASCII SHA256 hex characters; versioned suffix for actual mutations

oracle: Native receipt set must include every ACK and only externally intended sequences. Replay committed sequences, then verify every seeded row/version/body and all 100 group invariants. Independent snapshots verify latest committed pair and an older untouched pair; UTC prior-ACK watermark check uses a documented 10ms guard.
namespace: New UUID schema per case; preserve failed schemas. Drop a successful schema only after actors stop and complete external exports are fsynced/verified. Base orders fixture remains unchanged and independently verified.
resources: One active backend per performance cell, 4 CPUs/6 GiB/no swap. Each Go actor has 1 CPU/512 MiB/no swap; 1 analytical actor alone or 3 actors with mutations. Whole-store counters include the retained immutable base fixture as well as mutable data, receipts, indexes, WAL and engine files.
limits: Single Docker VM, no HA/replica/sharding claim. Same-key multi-writer conflicts, arbitrary update effects, permanent deletes, verified OS-cold access, open-loop saturation, disk EIO/full and physical power-loss recovery are unqualified. CedarDB engine source is closed; inspect versioned public APIs, shipped configuration and pinned pgx/PostgreSQL source.
